title: Incomplete Case-Sensitivity Handling in Payment MAC Calculation Filter
description: The ECPay payment gateway integration in topup.rs performs parameter filtering for CheckMacValue with a strict case-sensitive check, while parameter sorting is case-insensitive. Casing variations in incoming webhook requests bypass parameter exclusion and corrupt SHA-256 MAC calculation.
root_cause: In apps/api/src/topup.rs, check_mac() filters parameters using .filter(|(k, _)| k != "CheckMacValue"), which is strictly case-sensitive. While parameters are subsequently sorted case-insensitively using k.to_lowercase(), any casing variation of CheckMacValue (such as checkmacvalue, Checkmacvalue, or CHECKMACVALUE) bypasses the exclusion filter and is incorrectly included in the SHA-256 MAC calculation payload. Furthermore, param(&params, "CheckMacValue") in verified_form() uses exact case matching, which fails to find any case-varied parameter in the incoming webhook form.
intended_behavior: The CheckMacValue parameter exclusion and lookup should be case-insensitive, ensuring that any casing variation of CheckMacValue is excluded from MAC calculation and correctly extracted from webhook payloads.

trace.description: Receives URL-encoded form payload containing payment notification parameters from the payment provider.
Extracts CheckMacValue using case-sensitive lookup and passes params to check_mac for validation.
Filters parameters with k != "CheckMacValue" without case-insensitive matching, allowing case variations into MAC digest calculation.

evidence.description: Filter uses strictly case-sensitive inequality check: k != "CheckMacValue".
param() lookup uses exact case string equality: n == k.

conditions.description: Incoming HTTP POST webhook received at /api/v1/topups/webhook/{provider}.

execution.attacker_perspective: External client or payment gateway webhook sending payment notification parameters with varied key casing.
instructions: Submit a form-urlencoded POST request to /api/v1/topups/webhook/ecpay with lowercase checkmacvalue parameter name.
Observe that checkmacvalue is not excluded and is concatenated into MAC calculation payload HashKey=...&checkmacvalue=...&HashIV=...
Observe signature verification failure (401 UNAUTHORIZED) due to checkmacvalue being included in calculated hash.
execution.observed_result: Signature verification fails with 401 UNAUTHORIZED due to checkmacvalue being included in the calculated hash.

remediation.strategy: Use case-insensitive comparison (!k.eq_ignore_ascii_case("CheckMacValue")) in check_mac() and case-insensitive lookup in param() when extracting CheckMacValue.

code_changes.fixed_code: let mut p: Vec<&(String, String)> = params.iter().filter(|(k, _)| !k.eq_ignore_ascii_case("CheckMacValue")).collect();

likelihood.reason: Payment gateways, HTTP serializers, or reverse proxies commonly alter parameter casing in HTTP POST requests, or attackers can intentionally send lowercase keys.

impact.reason: Payment confirmation notifications fail MAC validation, resulting in topup failures or denial of service on payment confirmation callbacks.

confidence.reason: Confirmed via source code inspection in topup.rs showing case-sensitive string matching against case-insensitive ECPay parameter specification.

title: Unbounded In-Memory Buffer in Media Upload Confirmation Handler
description: In the upload confirmation endpoint, the S3 GET response is read directly into memory via res.bytes().await if the Content-Length header is omitted or chunked, creating a denial-of-service vector through excessive memory allocation.
root_cause: In apps/api/src/uploads.rs confirm(), the server checks object size with res.content_length().is_some_and(|l| l as usize > MAX_BYTES). If upstream S3 or object storage returns a response without Content-Length or uses chunked transfer encoding, this check evaluates to false. Subsequently, res.bytes().await reads the entire response body into heap memory without an upper bound limit, unlike avatar_bytes() which streams chunks and enforces MAX_BYTES dynamically.
intended_behavior: The confirm handler should stream chunks and enforce the 5MB size limit progressively during transfer, aborting the connection if total bytes exceed MAX_BYTES.

trace.description: Receives confirm request with object_key from authenticated user.
Inspects res.content_length() which is None for chunked transfer or omitted length headers, bypassing the MAX_BYTES check.
Invokes res.bytes().await without streaming limits, buffering arbitrary payload into server memory.

evidence.description: Size check only runs when Content-Length is Some: res.content_length().is_some_and(|l| l as usize > MAX_BYTES).
Unbounded buffering into memory: let bytes = res.bytes().await.

conditions.description: Requires an authenticated user session to obtain presigned upload URL and trigger confirm.

execution.attacker_perspective: Authenticated user uploading oversized object to S3 incoming folder.
instructions: Upload large file (e.g. 100MB+) to S3 incoming key using chunked transfer encoding.
Call POST /api/v1/uploads/confirm with the corresponding object_key.
Observe backend process allocating full file size in memory before image decoder validation.
execution.observed_result: Server process memory usage spikes proportional to uploaded file size, risking out-of-memory termination.

remediation.strategy: Adopt the chunked streaming pattern used in avatar_bytes() to stream S3 GET responses and enforce the 5MB MAX_BYTES threshold incrementally as chunks arrive.

code_changes.fixed_code: let mut bytes = Vec::new(); while let Some(chunk) = res.chunk().await.map_err(|_| AppError::problem(502, "UPSTREAM_ERROR", "儲存服務暫時無法使用"))? { if bytes.len() + chunk.len() > MAX_BYTES { return Err(AppError::invalid("/object_key", "IMAGE_REJECTED", "檔案超過 5 MB")); } bytes.extend_from_slice(&chunk); }

likelihood.reason: An authenticated user can easily generate a presigned PUT URL and upload an arbitrarily large file to S3 before calling the confirm endpoint.

impact.reason: Triggering unbounded memory allocation in the API process can lead to memory exhaustion, Linux OOM killer termination, and Denial of Service for all concurrent users.

confidence.reason: Verified in source code contrasting confirm() implementation against avatar_bytes() in the same module.

title: Inconsistent Protocol Scheme Handling in Native Client External Navigation
description: The desktop client intercepts target=_blank links and passes them directly to the native opener plugin without frontend protocol validation, creating discrepancies with Tauri capability allowlists and inconsistent handling between web and desktop platforms.
root_cause: In apps/web/app/plugins/native.client.ts, the global link interceptor for a[target="_blank"] forwards any non-origin URL to openExternal(a.href). While the native Tauri capabilities file (apps/web/src-tauri/capabilities/default.json) limits opener:allow-open-url to https, mailto, sms, and line schemes, standard http: links and custom scheme navigation in non-Tauri / hybrid web environments lack consistent validation before invocation, leading to unhandled runtime errors on valid http links or unexpected external protocol handlers.
intended_behavior: External URLs should be validated against an explicit scheme allowlist (e.g. https:, http:, mailto:, sms:, line:) before being forwarded to openExternal, with graceful error handling if an unsupported scheme is encountered.

trace.description: Intercepts click events on external target=_blank anchor tags.
Passes raw anchor href to openExternal without scheme allowlist validation.
Dispatches URL to Tauri opener plugin or window.open.

evidence.description: openExternal is called directly on arbitrary a.href without frontend scheme sanitization.
Opener allowlist permits https://*, mailto:*, sms:*, line://* but omits http://*.

conditions.description: User clicks an external link rendered in the web or desktop application.

execution.attacker_perspective: User providing an external item link or wishlist note containing an unallowed or unusual URI scheme.
instructions: Render an item link with http:// URL in the desktop client.
Observe unhandled plugin permission error from Tauri plugin-opener.
execution.observed_result: Link opening fails in desktop client due to strict capabilities mismatch, with no graceful fallback or prior scheme validation.

remediation.strategy: Sanitize and validate URL schemes in native.client.ts and native.ts before dispatching to openExternal, and align Tauri opener capabilities with permitted application protocols.

likelihood.reason: Requires user interaction clicking external links with non-https schemes.

impact.reason: Desktop client rejects http links causing navigation failures, or inconsistent scheme handling across web/desktop targets.

confidence.reason: Verified frontend link handler and Tauri capabilities configuration in src-tauri.
